name: Anterior Segment Developmental Anomaly of Genetic Origin

criteria.description: Presence of congenital corneal opacity or clouding
Iris hypoplasia, corectopia, or coloboma detected on slit-lamp examination
Identification of pathogenic variant in known anterior segment developmental genes (e.g., PAX6, FOXC1, PITX2)
Abnormalities in anterior chamber angle structures observed by gonioscopy or imaging
Positive family history of anterior segment anomalies or related ocular malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least two major criteria including corneal opacity or iris malformation, with or without genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended but not mandatory for diagnosis. Clinical examination remains primary.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically present at birth or early infancy

common.notes: Leads to impaired aqueous humor drainage
searchTerms: angle dysgenesis causing eye pressure issues

common.notes: Light sensitivity due to iris abnormalities
Range from mild to severe depending on anomaly extent

occasional.notes: Abnormal blood vessel growth into cornea
Displacement of the lens due to anterior segment defects
Involuntary eye movements secondary to visual impairment

searchTerms: cloudy lens after surgery or trauma

laboratory: Genetic testing identifying mutations in PAX6, FOXC1, PITX2, CYP1B1 genes
imaging: Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) showing angle and iris abnormalities
Ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM) for detailed anterior chamber evaluation
genetic: Autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance patterns depending on gene involved
Pathogenic variants in developmental transcription factors
other: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing corneal and iris malformations

distinguishingFeatures: Central corneal opacity with iridocorneal adhesions
Prominent Schwalbe line and iris strands
Systemic features such as dental and facial anomalies

redFlags: Rapidly increasing intraocular pressure indicating secondary glaucoma
Progressive visual loss in infancy or early childhood
Corneal perforation or severe corneal edema
references: Traboulsi EI. Genetic Diseases of the Eye. 2nd ed. Oxford University Press; 2012.
